sourcePolicy: Read-only metadata extraction from the archived selected configurations; no solver reruns or changed physical values.
title: What differs between the reconstructions?
cmeAnswer: Claude’s selected reconstruction includes explicit hydrodynamic cone CMEs. The selected Argon and Codex reconstructions use ambient wind without explicit CME injection. All three can also form compressions where fast streams catch slower wind.
frontInterpretation: A bright arc is a region of high plotted proton flux. Its appearance alone does not identify a CME, a shock or a unique eruption. Stream interactions and injected cones can both produce moving compressions.
scope: The views share clocks, units, exposure integration and plotting conventions. They retain different forcing, thermal closures, calibration histories, grids and saved surfaces. The comparison does not isolate the effect of any one modeling choice.
clockNote: Movies use geometric physical UTC. Quantitative X-ray comparisons use photon-arrival UTC and the same accepted EPIC-pn good-time intervals.
samplingNote: Comet curves use each model’s three-dimensional moving probe, including its out-of-plane position. Movie panels are selected two-dimensional surfaces and need not show the local value at the plotted comet marker.

argon.name: Argon
argon.cmeLabel: Ambient wind; no explicit CME injection
argon.cmeDetail: Both the fine comet reference and the coarser movie run disable cone injection. A separate 16-cone sensitivity run exists; it does not supply the displayed reference or movie.
argon.boundary: One rotating WSA map, with spacecraft-based speed and density corrections
argon.moviePlane: Solar-latitude −6.455° cone projected into ecliptic axes
argon.comparisonNote: The movie is a different, coarser run from the fine comet series.

codex.name: Codex
codex.cmeLabel: Ambient wind; no explicit CME injection
codex.cmeDetail: The selected constrained-transport reference has zero cone rows. Separate 12-hour and 24-hour cone controls are sensitivity cases; they do not supply this reference or movie.
codex.boundary: Evolving WSA/GONG boundary with calibrated normalizations and compatible magnetic edge electric fields
codex.comparisonNote: The retained 512 × 512 movie raster interpolates the selected three-dimensional solver state.

claude.name: Claude
claude.cmeLabel: Ambient wind with DONKI cone CMEs
claude.cmeDetail: The selected reference injects hydrodynamic cones from a filtered DONKI catalogue. The input file contains 121 catalogue rows; 74 pass the solver’s run-time loading interval. These are not 74 eruptions during the movie. The cones prescribe speed, density and temperature without a magnetic flux rope or ion charge-state model.
claude.boundary: Daily WSA maps with time-dependent speed and density corrections inferred from spacecraft
claude.temporalBoundary: Evolving coronal maps and explicit cone transients
claude.comparisonNote: The saved plane contains radial speed, so its colour represents radial proton flux rather than nₚ |v|.

values.claude: Evolving coronal maps and explicit cone transients
